episode: 1. Introduction to RAG - Why AI Needs an Open Book
learning_objectives: Recognize consequences of outdated and generic AI responses.
Understand the concept of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Explain how RAG addresses AI's "closed-book" problem.
outline: Challenges: Outdated knowledge, Hallucinations, Generic responses
Introducing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) as a solution
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Generative AI tools like ChatGPT, and familiarity with using the internet.

slides.title: The Magic of Generative AI
content: You've used tools like ChatGPT or Gemini.
They write poems, code, answer questions.
slides.narration:
You've probably used Generative AI tools.
Like **ChatGPT** or **Gemini**.
They feel like magic, don't they?
They write poems.
They write code.
They answer complex questions easily.
slides.image_prompt: A user happily interacting with a glowing AI chatbot interface, maybe with some magical sparkles and text bubbles showing diverse outputs (poem, code snippet, answer).

slides.title: A Hidden Flaw: "Closed-Book"
content: But they have a huge, hidden flaw.
slides.narration:
But these tools have a huge flaw.
It is often hidden.
They are "closed-book."
Think about it.
slides.image_prompt: A large, heavy book with a padlock on it, next to a glowing AI icon looking puzzled. The book is titled 'Knowledge'.

slides.title: The "Closed-Book" Analogy
content: Now they are locked in a room.
slides.narration:
Imagine a brilliant student.
This student has read many books.
But their study session ended.
It ended in 2024.
Now they are locked in a room.
They get no new information.
slides.image_prompt: A smart-looking student sitting at a desk, surrounded by stacks of books. The door behind them is clearly locked and barred. A calendar on the wall shows '2024'.

slides.title: Problem 1: Outdated Knowledge
slides.narration:
This "closed-book" problem causes major headaches.
First, the AI is **Outdated**.
It doesn't know yesterday's news.
It misses your company's latest report.
It cannot tell you a stock's current price.
Its knowledge is static.
slides.image_prompt: A newspaper with a very old date, a clock stuck in time, and an AI icon looking confused at a rapidly changing stock ticker or a blank news screen.

slides.title: Problem 2: Hallucinations
content: AI predicts the next most likely word.
If it doesn't know, it invents an answer.
slides.narration:
Second, it **Hallucinates**.
This means it makes stuff up.
An AI's job is to predict the next word.
If it doesn't know an answer, it invents one.
This invented answer often sounds correct.
But it is false.
This is a "hallucination."
It makes the AI unreliable for facts.
slides.image_prompt: An AI icon with question marks above its head, then speech bubbles containing clearly absurd or fantastical "facts" (e.g., "The moon is made of cheese"). A large red 'X' over the absurd facts.

slides.title: Problem 3: Generic Responses
content: AI has no idea who you are.
slides.narration:
Third, the AI is **Generic**.
It has no idea who you are.
It hasn't read your company's private files.
It doesn't know your team's wiki.
It cannot summarize your specific **PDF**.
It lacks domain specificity.
slides.image_prompt: A generic AI icon trying to read a very specific, confidential company document, looking confused or bored. Next to it, a pile of personal documents or a 'Private' folder icon.

slides.title: The Solution: Open the Book!
content: This course teaches you how to fix this.
Give that brilliant student a key to the library.
New rule: "Before you answer, look up the facts."
slides.narration:
This course teaches you how to fix this.
We will give that brilliant student a key.
A key to the library.
This library is your data.
We add a new rule.
"Before you answer, look up the facts."
slides.image_prompt: The brilliant student from before, now smiling, holding a large golden key, looking towards an open library door filled with glowing data and documents. The door is labeled 'Your Data'.

slides.title: Introducing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
slides.narration:
This "open-book" approach has a name.
It is called **Retrieval-Augmented Generation**.
We call it **RAG**.
You will learn about **RAG** in this series.
slides.image_prompt: A clear diagram showing an AI chatbot connected to a database or knowledge base. Arrows indicate 'Retrieval' of information before 'Generation' of a response. The acronym 'RAG' is prominently displayed.

slides.title: Summary
content: We learned about Generative AI's "closed-book" problem.
This causes outdated, hallucinated, and generic responses.
RAG helps AI access new, relevant facts.
slides.narration:
With this, we come to the end of this tutorial.
Let us summarise.
We learned about Generative AI's "closed-book" problem.
This causes outdated, hallucinated, and generic responses.
We introduced **Retrieval-Augmented Generation** or **RAG**.
**RAG** helps AI access new, relevant facts.

content: Think of a time an AI gave you an outdated answer.
Or perhaps it made something up.
Consider how having access to your specific data could have improved it.
